model_interpretation.claim: The earlier AVX-512 lane-state implementation was correct on five recorded correctness patterns and measured a mean of about 0.990 microseconds, versus the baseline mean of about 4.463 microseconds. These observations motivate testing a contrasting boundary and tuple-update strategy, but do not predict its result.
model_interpretation.applicability: The recorded timings and correctness cases used one thread and n=8192; they do not establish performance across sizes or patterns.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Have the controller validate this masked-tail, sentinel-initialized variant and compare its repeated timings under the same frozen protocol.

model_interpretation.claim: The previously measured lane-state kernel seeds from a full first vector and uses scalar handling for short inputs and the tail. Initializing each lane to the sentinel tuple (INT_MAX, INT_MAX), processing every full vector, and using one masked final vector should remove those special paths while preserving signed value-first, earliest-index ordering, including INT32_MAX. The per-vector tuple comparisons add work, so this tests whether simpler boundary handling offsets that cost; no speedup is assumed.

items.subject: One-pass AVX-512 lane minima with earliest-index state
items.objective: Explore a one-pass AVX-512 lane-state argmin: keep each lane's signed minimum and earliest absolute index across successive 16-element vectors, then combine lane results using value-first and index-second ordering. Handle the initial block and scalar tail correctly, including INT32_MAX, INT32_MIN and ties. Stay within the supplied thread budget; compare correctness and repeated timings against the baseline.
